A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gender inequality is not simply the result of the gendered division of labor, but is the result of a complex interplay between gender and the organization of work.
gender inequality in earnings is not only the result of gender differences in human capital, but also the result of gendered processes of exploitation and opportunity.
the relational model of gender earnings inequality in manufacturing workplaces provides an alternative and more comprehensive explanation of gender earnings inequality than the human capital model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the local gender wage gap is not simply a function of the gender composition of the labor market.
gender inequality is a function of the interaction of local gender politics and workplace-level dynamics.
the relational model of wage inequality is a useful tool to examine gender inequality and to understand how gender politics shape the local production of gender inequality.
